text.insert: ProjectSession owns the project worktree, head_revision, and ordered timeline from baseline preparation through explicit close. Sync is its operator-initiated intake-and-reconciliation workflow: observation records a request, the operator starts the dispatch handoff, reconciliation stays isolated in staging, and confirm-gated publication advances the durable boundary. This section relates that workflow to epoch, PR, remote_application, knowledge-revision, and save-point evidence while scheduling and shipping remain in their owning sections.

Session operating flow covers the first-read ProjectSession path, including the operator-started sync handoff from a requested observation through drain, staging, validation, publication or cancellation, and explicit session close.

Project session architecture covers the durable container, the single-active-session rule, the nine sync statuses, and the dispatch-lease boundary that keeps reconciliation staging separate from the session worktree until publish.

Save points covers evidence anchors pinned to existing commits, including the post-publication sync boundary anchor, while remote_application and knowledge revision records preserve the transactional lineage that created that head.
